title: Prove Dashboard session workspace choices in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: SEED-413#prove-session-workspace-starts-on-vitest (.planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md), plan 848, revision 29d112fbe44d809896f3826e3f14ba9933538db7 (product and test content identical to cc799350b).

Promise: first key example. A developer selects the execution checkout with existing changes; Start presents the current changes for confirmation and dispatches nothing until they are confirmed.

Validation of the suggestions:
- Fault location: kept on the `unconfirmedStart` path in dashboard/server/launchStart.ts. launchPreAcceptance.ts `preAcceptanceAnswer` delegates its existing-changes answer to `unconfirmedStart` (launchPreAcceptance.ts line 113), so one edit there faults both. I chose the stale variant of the suggestion because it is the subtle one; an absent fingerprint is the request's ordinary unconfirmed shape.
- Fault applied (one line, launchStart.ts line 120):
  `if (found !== undefined && found.fingerprint !== request.existingChanges)` became
  `if (found !== undefined && request.existingChanges === undefined)`.
  Any supplied fingerprint, stale or not, then counts as confirmed.
- Focused command: kept as suggested. The spec is a Node Vitest spec, and scripts/test-backend.mjs sends it to Vitest. `--workers=1` is accepted. The strict reporter was used, without --reporter=list:
  `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:backend -- --workers=1 dashboard/backend-tests/launches/ad-hoc-existing-changes-start.spec.ts`

Assertion that caught it: dashboard/backend-tests/launches/ad-hoc-existing-changes-start.spec.ts, test "existing changes answer their current fingerprint, keeping nothing, until a Start confirms it" (line 133). It failed at line 146, `expect(found).toEqual([found[0], found[0], found[0]])`. The third request carried the stale fingerprint "0".repeat(64). It received `undefined` where the current existing-changes answer was expected (kind existing-changes, count 4, four paths). That is the observed wrong path: a stale confirmation let Start through unconfirmed. The claim is limited to the stale-fingerprint path through `unconfirmedStart` on a borrowed default checkout with a real dirty Git checkout.

Setup and reach:
- Scratch checkout: a detached git worktree of 29d112fbe at /tmp/intent-cov-848.isID/co, clean before the probe. `npm ci` ran on Node v24.21.0. The execution checkout was not edited.
- Baseline (two runs, load average 30 to 47): the selected test passed both times (3097 ms in the second run). The two confirmed-Start tests (lines 160 and 178) timed out at the default 5000 ms in both runs (about 5.1 s each). These tests do not exercise the faulted branch.
- Independent witness: a scratch Vitest file (untracked, deleted afterwards) built its own dirty borrowed checkout and called `unconfirmedStart` directly.
  - Unfaulted: absent fingerprint returned existing-changes; stale returned existing-changes.
  - Faulted: absent returned existing-changes; stale returned none. So Start would proceed without confirming the current changes.
  - The witness did not reach `preAcceptanceAnswer`, because that call needs a configured project ("Unknown configured project: open-dough"). Its delegation to `unconfirmedStart` was confirmed by reading the code.
- Faulted run: 3 failed, 1 passed. The selected test failed on the assertion above. The two confirmed-Start tests timed out as in the baseline. The unrelated schema test passed.
- Restoration: a shell EXIT trap copied back the original launchStart.ts. `git diff --quiet HEAD` reported clean and the witness file was removed. The pre-probe state was clean. On the restored rerun the selected test passed again (2334 ms) and the confirmed-Start tests timed out again as in the baseline. The scratch worktree was then removed.

Separate observation (not caused by the fault; repair decision stays with the caller): the confirmed review Start test (line 160) and the confirmed auto-land Start test (line 178) exceeded Vitest's default 5000 ms timeout in all four local runs at load average 30 to 51. Branch CI on cc799350b (run 45791889476) succeeded. Per the project's local = CI and failures-under-load rules, this needs a classification by the caller (load-sensitive tests running near the default timeout). The probe gives no verdict on those tests' assertions.

Next proof action: none for this promise's stale-confirmation path; the maintained assertion catches it. Optionally probe the absent-fingerprint variant, which the same test's first two requests appear to cover. That variant was not faulted here.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest "Duration" for the focused file): baseline 18.05 s and 29.44 s; faulted 24.34 s; restored 27.35 s. Scratch witness test bodies took 4.7 to 5.8 s per run (Vitest per-test time). All runs were at load average 30 to 51.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human interaction occurred during the probe and no separate measure exists.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported token or turn measure is available to this agent.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 294709 ms (measured), from 1795686691529 to 1795686986238 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition (checked revision 29d112fbe44d809896f3826e3f14ba9933538db7):
- Verdict Caught. The stale-confirmation path needs no new or stronger proof.
- Separate observation: the confirmed review and auto-land Start cases in `ad-hoc-existing-changes-start.spec.ts` exceeded the 5000 ms default in four local runs at load average 30–51, while branch CI run 45791889476 passed them.
  - Decision: this is a load-sensitive test cost. It fits the queued retrospective correction's outcome.
  - Action: extended slice 1 of [Restore dropped session workspace proof](seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#restore-session-workspace-vitest-proof) (plan 854) to reduce these near-limit cases' cost and rerun them under comparable load. One queue entry, which stays first.
